cards.title: The Winner’s Ceremony
cards.instruction: Treat every contest, bargain, or decision as incomplete until the proper recognition, ritual, and consequence have occurred.

beats.speaker: B

beats.text: With my name. The other passengers weren't watching.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a train seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then a brief announcement will suit the occasion perfectly.

beats.text: I won our coin toss. Please announce who sits by the window.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then announce my name from your seat. I'll approach when called.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The conductor needs to get past us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An official witness. Ask her to present the seat, and I'll accept it immediately.

cards.title: Everything Is Sudden Death

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I founded this club last month. Tonight's our first meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fresh founding date too. Shall I give the new members some history before we put it all behind us?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims shared cupboard knowledge; A3 treats B2's denial as modernization and A5 explains B4 as restoration.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 absorbs the never-existing piano; A5 specifically uses B4's gardening purpose to justify removing it.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 try to correct A's institutional memory while A keeps speaking as a member.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes even identification of the club confirm A's supposed historical understanding.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies a trophy cupboard and piano; B4 anchors the gardening club.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'original purpose' turns B4's correction into confident insider approval.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assumes shared trophy-storage history; A3 calls the contradiction modernization; A5 treats the club's recent founding as a revised founding date.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's shelf but sidesteps the piano denial; A5 directly converts B4's first-meeting fact into an opportunity to supply history.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects storage arrangements and B4 asserts founder authority; A5 responds by claiming the role of historical guide for B's members.

heightening.evidence: After B4 denies any earlier club history, A5 escalates from remembering a rose show to offering the new members an institutional history.

specificity.evidence: A1 provides a gardening trophy, cupboard and piano; B4's first meeting makes the already-existing trophy slightly curious but not contradictory.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Open shelving' neatly recasts correction as change; A5's 'fresh founding date' is earned, while 'put it all behind us' adds some flourish.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 replaces A's remembered cupboard with a shelf and denies the piano; A3 treats the corrected arrangement as modernization since A's supposed tenure.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 establishes that the founder started the club last month and this is its first meeting; A5 calls that a fresh founding date and offers history to its new members.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A maintains insider standing by treating contradictions as institutional changes rather than evidence of mistaken identity.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 answers the strongest contradiction by claiming authority to teach the very history B4 says cannot exist.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: S220 preserves assumed insider status by treating corrections to almost-plausible memories as evidence of institutional change.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Ordinary misremembering permits correction; A converts each correction into further evidence that the institution has changed.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 treats B2's shelf and absent piano as modernization; A5 treats B4's founding date as another revision and offers to supply the displaced history.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised the club setting to make B its founder at the first meeting. Separate internal pass: fidelity 5 (A3 and A5 explain contradictions as institutional change), logic 5 (B2's shelf becomes A3's modernization; B4's founding becomes A5's fresh date), relationship 4 (B2 directs storage and B4 asserts firsthand founding knowledge), heightening 4 (A5 offers to teach the nonexistent history), specificity 5 (A1's gardening trophy and B4's first meeting), brevity 4 (A5's history offer follows the disputed founding): 92. Spoken ABABA gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: The trophy at a first meeting leaves a small contextual question, and A3 does not specifically reinterpret the missing piano. Neither breaks the central progression. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A5 requires sincere belief that the club has restarted or rewritten its history; a knowing delivery would turn the scene into deliberate imposture.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved reunion alternative protects familial belonging against explicit exclusion. This alternative competes with a founder's account and turns false familiarity into an offer of institutional service.

cards.title: Insider with the Wrong Memories
cards.instruction: Act like an unquestioned insider while offering details that almost fit. Treat each contradiction as proof the group, system, or relationship changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At our old reunions, Uncle Frank always carved the turkey.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody here has an Uncle Frank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Families edit their history so quickly now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're at the wrong reunion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a remarkably efficient way to describe how much you've changed.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assumes shared reunions; A3 makes the missing uncle historical editing; A5 makes exclusion evidence of change.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 directly absorbs B2's absent Uncle Frank; A5 reinterprets B4's wrong-reunion diagnosis.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects family identity and B4 explicitly contests A's right to belong.

heightening.evidence: A5 survives B4's direct exclusion by treating the entire relationship's rejection as confirmation.

specificity.evidence: A1 gives Uncle Frank carving turkey at reunions, a plausible but misplaced family detail.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's efficient-description reading is directly earned by B4's categorical correction.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assumes shared reunion history; A3 calls the missing uncle edited history and A5 makes being at the wrong reunion evidence of the family's change.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's denial of Uncle Frank directly becomes A3's historical editing; B4's wrong-reunion correction becomes A5's reinterpretation of the relationship.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects a family claim and B4 challenges A's belonging altogether; A5 preserves intimacy by attributing the rejection to changes in B's group.

heightening.evidence: B4 moves from one nonexistent relative to A's entire mistaken presence; A5 absorbs that larger contradiction into the same insider certainty.

specificity.evidence: A1 gives Uncle Frank carving turkey at reunions, and B4 locates A at the wrong gathering; the relationship to this particular B remains implicit.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's edited-history explanation is concise, and A5 earns its reinterpretation from B4's direct challenge to A's presence.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 denies that anyone has Uncle Frank; A3 explains the missing relative as revision of family history.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 says A is at the wrong reunion; A5 treats that description as proof of how thoroughly the familiar group has changed.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A sustains unquestioned belonging by making every contradiction evidence against the group's continuity.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 protects the whole imagined relationship after B4 escalates beyond disputing a single remembered detail.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: S220 maintains unquestioned belonging by recasting increasingly direct memory contradictions as changes in the family itself.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: A deliberate impostor might knowingly bluff; A sincerely treats the family's denials as alterations to shared history.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 attributes B2's denial to edited history, and A5 treats B4's exclusion as changed family behavior.

records.recommendedEdit: Retained unchanged because B4 sharply increases the threat to insider status and A5 develops the exact same defense. Internal rereading confirms the ratings.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed for an internal pass. A3 is somewhat aphoristic, and A5 develops interpretive commitment rather than a new practical demand.
records.writerReservation: A3 and A5 can sound knowingly accusatory; sincerity is essential to distinguish mistaken belonging from deliberate deception.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b escalates from a plausible family memory to a challenge to belonging; a remains a lower-pressure dispute about club furnishings.
